issue: Goodwill impairment and indefinite-lived intangible impairment are BAR content under the CPA Evolution Blueprints (carried into 2026), but most of this module's goodwill and indefinite-lived material is not marked optional. The P2-2 decision was also applied inconsistently. far-imp-04, -05 and -08 are optional, while far-imp-13, -14, -29 and -30 are the same goodwill computation and are not. As a result, BAR material counts toward FAR practice, readiness and the study plan, and the TBS scores three BAR cells.
evidence: Optional: far-imp-04 (goodwill cap), far-imp-05 (goodwill cap), far-imp-08 (PCC alternative). Not optional but the same BAR content: goodwill: far-imp-07 (testing order vs. goodwill), -13, -14, -29, -30 (cap computations), -15 (qualitative screen), -18 (annual test), -20 (interim trigger), fc4, fc6. Indefinite-lived intangibles: far-imp-03, -16, -23, -31, fc3. TBS rows loss.rl (radio license), loss.tn (trade name) and loss.gw (goodwill) are 3 of the 9 scored cells. The lesson states objective 2 as "Measure impairment for ... indefinite-lived intangibles, and goodwill" (task "Calculate goodwill and intangible asset impairment") and has full Indefinite-lived and Goodwill sections, with no scope note. Cross-module: far-int-16 (PCC goodwill alternative) is not optional, but its twin far-imp-08 is. Scope evidence: review/reference/far-standards.md §1c lists "Goodwill and indefinite-lived intangibles — No (BAR, per Becker)"; review/reference/blueprint-notes.md says FAR Area II F is "Finite-lived only: goodwill, indefinite-lived intangibles ... are BAR". Web search: SuperfastCPA files "Calculating Goodwill Impairment Losses" under BAR content area 2, Technical Accounting and Reporting (https://www.superfastcpa.com/?p=97096), and files FAR intangibles questions as "Carrying Amount of Finite-Lived Intangible Assets" (https://www.superfastcpa.com/?p=95014).
source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (eff. 1/1/2026): BAR Area II (indefinite-lived intangible assets, including goodwill); FAR Area II.F (intangible assets, finite-lived). REVIEW.md P2-2.
fix: Apply P2-2 consistently: mark far-imp-03, -07, -13, -14, -15, -16, -18, -20, -23, -29, -30, -31, fc3, fc4 and fc6 optional (and far-int-16 in far-intangibles). In the lesson, put the Indefinite-lived and Goodwill sections under a "BAR scope (optional for FAR)" callout, and reword objective 2 to cover held for sale only. In the TBS, replace the rl, tn and gw rows with FAR rows: a held-for-sale write-down, a finite-lived intangible tested under ASC 360, and next-year depreciation on the new cost basis. A TBS cannot be partly optional. If the team instead confirms that goodwill is FAR, unmark far-imp-04, -05 and -08 and remove the P2-2 entry. Either way, keep the flags consistent.

issue: Two pure-recall items are labeled skill "analysis" and difficulty 3. That is two skill levels too high, and it inflates the module's analysis count, which feeds the Blueprint skill-mix targets.
evidence: far-imp-27: "An impaired asset held and used recovers in fair value the next year. What happens?" The key is "No reversal", which recalls one rule (ASC 360-10-35-20) and is also tested by far-imp-11 (remembering/1). far-imp-21: "A company plans to abandon a machine in 6 months. How is it accounted for?" The key is "As held and used", which recalls one rule (ASC 360-10-45-15). Neither stem gives data to examine or interrelate. Both are labeled analysis/3.
source: AICPA Blueprint skill definitions (Remembering and Understanding vs. Analysis); src/content/schema.ts skill and difficulty fields
fix: Relabel both remembering, difficulty 1. Alternatively, rewrite them as real analysis items: for example, give a machine to be abandoned with its cost, prior depreciation and revised life, and ask for current-year depreciation and the classification.

issue: Skill and difficulty labels are off by one level. Items 22-31 are uniformly labeled analysis/3, but each is a single application of one formula. Items 19, 20 and 23 are pure recall labeled application. The same computation is labeled differently in two places.
evidence: Application labeled analysis/3: 22 (900/950/700, UCF > CA so 0), 24 (500-380 = 120,000), 25 (520 > 500 so 0), 26 (300-(280-15) = 35,000), 28 (min(50,35) = 35,000), 29 (min(100,200) = 100,000), 30 (min(100,50) = 50,000), 31 (200-170 = 30,000, trivial at difficulty 3). Recall labeled application: 19 (finite-lived intangibles use recoverability then fair value), 20 (a major adverse change is a trigger), 23 (the qualitative screen exists). Inconsistent: far-x2-10 has the same numbers as far-imp-24 and is labeled application/2, but 24 is analysis/3. cues.md reports 11 analysis labels among 33 practice and exam items. After relabeling, the module has no genuine analysis-level item, against the FAR target of 35-45%.
source: AICPA Blueprint skill definitions; content/sections/far.yaml skillAllocation
fix: Relabel 22, 24, 25, 26, 28, 29 and 30 as application, difficulty 2; 31 as application, difficulty 1; and 19, 20 and 23 as remembering. To keep analysis coverage, add 2-3 real analysis items. Examples: identify the asset group from cash-flow interdependence; choose among held-for-sale, held-and-used and abandoned with multi-period effects; reconcile a fixed-asset schedule after an impairment.

issue: The explanations do not teach. Many distractor explanations are just "Not the computation." and never say which error produces the number. The item-level explanations state the rule but show no computation.
evidence: Each "Not the computation." distractor and the error that actually produces it (reproduced in python): 22(b) 250,000 = UCF 950,000 - FV 700,000; 24(c) 70,000 = UCF 450,000 - FV 380,000; 25(c) 20,000 = UCF - CA; 25(d) 140,000 = UCF 520,000 - FV 380,000; 26(b) 15,000 = costs to sell only; 28(d) 15,000 = 50,000 - 35,000 (the recovery above the cap); 29(d) 300,000 = excess 100,000 + goodwill 200,000; 30(d) 150,000 = excess + goodwill; 31(b) 170,000 = fair value as the loss; 31(c) 200,000 = full write-off. Item-level explanations without numbers: 13 ("goodwill impairment = CA - FV, not exceeding goodwill"), 14, 17 ("allocate pro rata", with no 300/500 x 100 = 60,000), 22, 24, 25, 26 (no 280 - 15 = 265), 28, 29, 30, 31. Compare far-imp-03, -05 and far-x2-10, which show the full computation.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 4 (explanations state the rule and show the computation)
fix: Replace each "Not the computation." with the error it models, for example 24(c): "70,000 subtracts fair value from undiscounted cash flows; those cash flows only test recoverability." Rewrite each item-level explanation to show the steps, for example 26: "FV less cost to sell = 280,000 - 15,000 = 265,000; loss = 300,000 - 265,000 = 35,000."

issue: Distractor (d) $200,000 is labeled outdated-rule, and its explanation blames the old implied-goodwill Step 2. Step 2 cannot produce $200,000 from this stem, so the rationale names an error that does not generate the number.
evidence: The stem gives a carrying amount of 5,000,000 (goodwill 800,000) and a fair value of 4,600,000. Pre-ASU 2017-04 Step 2 needs the fair value of the unit's identifiable net assets, which the stem does not give. Using carrying amounts as a proxy, implied goodwill = 4,600,000 - 4,200,000 = 400,000 and the loss = 800,000 - 400,000 = 400,000, which is the key. No rule-based error gives 200,000.
fix: Add "the fair value of the unit's identifiable net assets is $4,400,000" to the stem and change (d) to $600,000 (old Step 2: implied goodwill 200,000; 800,000 - 200,000 = 600,000), keeping outdated-rule. Alternatively, change (d) to $1,200,000 (excess + goodwill) with trap wrong-rule.

issue: Some trap labels do not match the misconception the distractor models, and the same error is labeled differently from item to item.
evidence: 05(c) 300,000 = excess 1,200,000 - goodwill 900,000 is labeled "reversed"; the same error is "wrong-rule" in 14(b) and 04(c). 24(b) 50,000 and x2-10(a) 50,000 (CA - UCF, the recoverability gap) are labeled "wrong-rule"; the same error is "partial-computation" in chk1(a), 09(b) and x2-29(a). 18(a) "Only when a triggering event occurs" and 23(c) "Only for goodwill, not intangibles" are labeled "partial-computation" on non-numeric items; they model incomplete-rule or scope errors (wrong-rule or wrong-classification).
fix: 05(c) -> wrong-rule; 24(b) and x2-10(a) -> partial-computation; 18(a) -> wrong-rule; 23(c) -> wrong-classification.

issue: Answer cues: in each item the key is the only qualified, hedged option and is much longer than the others, while the distractors are bare or absolute.
evidence: chk2: the key is "A held-for-sale asset, up to prior losses", the only option with a qualifier. The others are bare asset names ("Goodwill of a reporting unit", "A factory held and used", "An indefinite-lived trademark"). 18: the key is "At least annually, and between tests if triggered". The distractors are "Only when a triggering event occurs", "Every three years" and "Only when the business is sold", with absolutes in (a) and (d). cues.md flags both items as "key much longest".
fix: chk2: give the distractors parallel qualifiers ("Goodwill, up to the original balance", "A factory held and used, up to the prior loss", "An indefinite-lived trademark, through OCI"). 18: use parallel-length options, such as "Annually only, on a fixed date", "Only when a triggering event occurs, at the entity level", "At least annually, and between tests if triggered" and "Every three years, unless triggered sooner".

issue: Several distractors are implausible, or do not answer the question asked, so these items test elimination rather than knowledge.
evidence: 01(b) "A routine increase in accumulated depreciation" and (c) "Payment of a regular dividend". 20(c) "Paying a regular dividend" (the dividend filler again) and (d) "A 2% rise in quarterly revenue". 19(c) "It's never tested". 23(b) "Yes, always, with no assessment". 16(d) "Amortization of $90,000" answers a different question; the stem asks for the impairment loss.
fix: Use near-miss distractors from the indicator and qualitative-factor lists. For 01: "A current-period operating loss with no history of losses" (not by itself an indicator), or "A decline in fair value that is below carrying amount but above undiscounted cash flows" (an indicator only if significant). For 20: "A decline in the entity's share price that is not sustained". For 19: "Annual qualitative screen, then fair value only". For 23: "Yes, but only if the asset was acquired within the past year". For 16: "$950,000 write-up to fair value".

issue: Redundancy: the held-and-used two-step test is asked 8 times in the same form (pre1, chk1, 09, 22, 24, 25, x2-10, x2-29), plus the lesson's worked example and TBS rows eq and bl. far-imp-22 reuses the lesson's trap numbers verbatim, and far-imp-25 is far-imp-24 with only the undiscounted cash flows changed. Both reward memorizing numbers.
evidence: Lesson trap: "if undiscounted cash flows had been $950,000, there is no impairment", with CA 900,000 and FV 700,000. far-imp-22: CA 900,000, UCF 950,000, FV 700,000, key $0, identical. far-imp-24: 500,000/450,000/380,000, key 120,000. far-imp-25: 500,000/520,000/380,000, key 0; cues.md gives Jaccard 0.82. pre1 (500,000/540,000/420,000, key 0) already tests the "recoverable despite a lower FV" trap. That makes 3 items (pre1, 22, 25) that test that one trap with near-identical structure.
fix: Rewrite 22 and 25 to test untested ASC 360 rules: (i) next-year depreciation on the new cost basis (e.g., new basis 700,000 / 5 remaining years = 140,000); (ii) cash-flow horizon based on the remaining life of the primary asset; (iii) an impairment indicator present but the asset recoverable, followed by a revision of useful life. Keep pre1 as the trap item.

issue: The mock-exam item far-x2-10 is a clone of practice item far-imp-24: same facts, same numbers, same key and the same distractor amounts. A learner who has practiced sees an item already answered, which inflates the mock score as a readiness signal.
evidence: far-imp-24: "Equipment held and used has a $500,000 carrying amount, $450,000 of undiscounted cash flows and a $380,000 fair value", options 120,000/50,000/70,000/0, key 120,000. far-x2-10: "An asset group held and used has a carrying amount of $500,000, undiscounted future cash flows of $450,000, and a fair value of $380,000", options 50,000/0/70,000/120,000, key 120,000. The cross-bank finding F-0188 (S2) also flags this pair.
fix: Rewrite far-x2-10 with new numbers and a twist not drilled in practice. Example: an asset group with a $10,000 selling-cost distractor and a PV figure, CA 640,000, UCF 610,000, FV 520,000, PV 540,000, key 120,000. Alternatively, retire far-imp-24.

issue: Redundancy: "goodwill loss = reporting-unit CA - FV, capped at goodwill" is asked 6 times in this module in the same form, in two mirrored pairs (13/14 and 29/30), plus the lesson's faded example (3 steps), TBS row gw and far-x2-11.
evidence: Excess below goodwill: 04 (1.5M < 2.0M), 13 (400,000 < 800,000), 29 (100,000 < 200,000). Excess above goodwill, capped: 05 (1.2M -> 900,000), 14 (1.0M -> 800,000), 30 (100,000 -> 50,000). 13 and 14 share the stem and differ only in FV (Jaccard 0.76); 29 and 30 differ only in goodwill (0.87). The cross-bank finding F-0197 also flags this cluster.
fix: Keep one below-cap item (04) and one capped item (05). Retire 13, 14, 29 and 30, or rewrite them to test other goodwill rules if goodwill stays in scope (for example, the testing order with an asset-group impairment that changes the RU carrying amount). Under M-far-impairment-001 (BAR scope) these are and optional anyway.

issue: Redundancy: far-imp-11 and far-imp-27 test the identical fact ("no reversal of a held-and-used impairment") in the same way. The same rule is also the answer to chk2's option (b), far-imp-02's option (d) and fc5.
evidence: 11: "Under U.S. GAAP, may an impairment loss on an asset held and used be reversed if its fair value later recovers?", key "No". 27: "An impaired asset held and used recovers in fair value the next year. What happens?", key "No reversal". Both have reversal-up-to-the-loss and OCI distractors.
fix: Rewrite 27 as an application item. Example: equipment written down to 700,000 with 5 years remaining; next year its fair value rises to 800,000; ask for the carrying amount at the end of that year (700,000 - 140,000 = 560,000; no write-up).

issue: Lesson-item alignment: two practice items test rules the lesson never teaches. Held for sale, which four items compute with, gets no body section, only a flowchart box, one takeaway and a table row.
evidence: far-imp-17 tests pro-rata allocation of an asset-group loss by carrying amount, with no asset reduced below its determinable fair value (ASC 360-10-35-28). The lesson never mentions allocation, and the "asset group" concept (lowest level of largely independent cash flows, 360-10-35-23) is not defined. far-imp-21 tests that an asset to be abandoned stays held and used until abandoned, with depreciation revised (360-10-45-15, 360-10-35-47); the lesson does not mention abandonment. Held for sale: far-imp-06, -12, -26 and -28 require FV less cost to sell, no depreciation, and recovery limited to cumulative losses. The lesson gives these only as one-line rules, with no worked example and no classification criteria (360-10-45-9).
fix: Add a short "Held for sale" body section with the classification criteria and a worked example (write-down to FV less cost to sell, then a recovery capped at prior losses). Add 2-3 sentences on asset groups and pro-rata allocation (with the fair-value floor), and one sentence on assets to be abandoned (held and used until abandoned; revise depreciation).

issue: The lesson presents the one-step goodwill test as a public-entity rule: "For public business entities (ASU 2017-04)", the takeaway "Goodwill (public entities)" and fc4 "(public, ASU 2017-04)". ASU 2017-04 removed Step 2 for all entities. A private company that does not elect the PCC alternative uses the same one-step test, which the lesson leaves unclear.
evidence: ASU 2017-04 was effective for SEC filers for FY beginning after 12/15/2019 and for all other entities for FY beginning after 12/15/2022. It now applies to every entity that applies ASC 350-20 without the alternative. The lesson contrasts "public" only with "private companies may elect to amortize", which implies non-electing private companies follow some other model.
fix: Reword to "All entities (ASU 2017-04), unless a private company or NFP elects the goodwill alternative". Update the takeaway and fc4 to match.

issue: The lesson says "(IFRS permits reversals for assets other than goodwill — a common comparison question.)" IFRS-versus-U.S. GAAP differences have not been tested on FAR since the July 2021 Blueprint, so calling this "a common comparison question" for the 2026 exam is outdated.
evidence: Journal of Accountancy (Nov 2020) on the post-practice-analysis Blueprint: candidates "no longer will be tested on the differences between IFRS and U.S. GAAP" (https://www.journalofaccountancy.com/news/2020/nov/cpa-exam-refresh-after-practice-analysis/). Surgent lists the IFRS differences among FAR content removed in July 2021 (https://www.surgent.com/blog/cpa_exam_changes_2021/). The reference sheet (far-standards.md §1c) also says IFRS is "believed not tested".
source: AICPA Blueprint (July 2021 onward) as reported by the Journal of Accountancy and Surgent
fix: Delete the sentence, or reword it as "(For background only: IFRS permits reversals other than for goodwill; IFRS is not tested on the 2026 CPA Exam.)"

issue: Sequencing: far-impairment comes before far-intangibles in far.yaml, but the lesson and its items assume the learner already knows what goodwill, reporting units and indefinite-lived (versus finite-lived) intangibles are. Those are introduced only in the next module, and the intangibles lesson points back ("tested for impairment (see the impairment module)").
evidence: far.yaml u6 order: far-ppe-acquisition, far-depreciation, far-impairment, far-intangibles. The impairment lesson never defines goodwill, a reporting unit or an indefinite life. far-imp-03, -16, -19, -23, -31 and all the goodwill items depend on them. The far-intangibles lesson defines the finite/indefinite split and goodwill measurement.
fix: Either move far-impairment after far-intangibles in far.yaml, or add a 3-line primer at the top of the impairment lesson (goodwill = residual in an acquisition; reporting unit; indefinite-lived = no foreseeable limit to its cash flows) with a link to far-intangibles.

issue: The research part is not discriminating: each wrong excerpt covers a different asset class (indefinite-lived intangibles, goodwill, held for sale), so a candidate can eliminate them from the asset type alone, without reading the guidance.
evidence: The prompt asks why the held-and-used studio building is not impaired. Excerpts (a) 350-30, (c) 350-20 and (d) 360-10-35-43 (held for sale) cannot apply to a held-and-used building. Only (b) 360-10-35-17 is about held-and-used assets. The key is correct.
fix: Replace two distractors with near-miss held-and-used excerpts, such as 360-10-35-21 (indicators that trigger a test) and 360-10-35-20 (new cost basis; no restoration), so the candidate must distinguish the recoverability rule from related ASC 360 paragraphs.

issue: Option (d) is the text "$     0" (padded with spaces). HTML collapses whitespace, so it will render as "$ 0", which looks like a typo. It is also inconsistent with the "None ($0)" wording in far-x2-10 and the practice items.
evidence: far-exam-area2.json: "text": "$     0". The same padding appears in two other exam items in the area 1 and area 2 files.

issue: The stem says the asset's "fair value later rises by $50,000". The held-for-sale gain is measured on the increase in fair value less cost to sell (ASC 360-10-35-40). The key holds only if costs to sell are unchanged.
evidence: Key (a) 35,000 = min(50,000 increase, 35,000 cumulative loss). If costs to sell had also changed, the recognized increase would differ. The stem is silent on this.
fix: Reword to "...was written down by $35,000 to fair value less cost to sell; fair value less cost to sell later rises by $50,000."
